semaglutide.summary: Weekly GLP-1 medication that cuts appetite and drives large fat loss, leaning out the body and face together.

quick.overview:
Semaglutide is a GLP-1 medication sold as Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy. People use it to lose body fat quickly, and as total fat comes down the body and face lean out and puffiness drops.

It mimics the gut hormone GLP-1, which lowers hunger, increases fullness and slows stomach emptying, so calorie intake falls. In trials of adults with overweight or obesity, average loss was roughly 12 percent of body weight over 68 weeks or longer. It has no known way to target facial fat, so the face changes along with overall fat loss.
quick.how: It is given as a weekly injection (Ozempic, Wegovy) or a daily tablet (Rybelsus) under medical prescription. Users pair it with higher protein intake and resistance training to hold on to muscle while the scale drops. Weight loss builds over weeks to months, and weight is typically regained after stopping.
quick.risks: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are the most common effects; gallbladder disease and pancreatitis are rarer. The label carries a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumours seen in rodents. Fast, large weight loss can cause facial hollowing ("Ozempic face") and loss of lean mass. It is prescription-only, and compounded or grey-market versions raise separate quality concerns.

angle.text: Users take semaglutide to lose body fat quickly; as appetite drops and a calorie deficit builds, the body and face lean out and puffiness reduces. Weight loss is well studied in trials, while facial changes, including the hollowing some call "Ozempic face", are reported by users and in case discussions.

tirzepatide.summary: Weekly GIP/GLP-1 injection with the largest average weight losses reported for an approved drug, leaning out body and face.

quick.overview:
Tirzepatide is a weekly injectable sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound. People use it to cut body fat, and the face leans out as weight comes off.

It activates both GIP and GLP-1 receptors, which lowers appetite and calorie intake. In the SURMOUNT-1 trial, average weight change at 72 weeks was about -15.0, -19.5 and -20.9 percent across the three studied strengths, among the largest reductions reported for an approved anti-obesity drug. Facial leaning follows total fat loss, and with larger losses, facial volume loss and skin laxity can be more noticeable in some users.
quick.how: It is prescribed as a once-weekly injection, with the amount stepped up gradually by the prescriber. Users combine it with high protein intake and resistance training to preserve muscle. Results build over months, and weight returns after stopping.
quick.risks: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are common, mostly while the amount is being increased. Pancreatitis, gallbladder disease and dehydration-related kidney injury have been reported, and the label carries a thyroid C-cell tumour warning. It can reduce the effectiveness of oral contraceptives. Lean mass is lost along with fat. It is prescription-only; unregulated peptide-vial sources add contamination and accuracy risks.

angle.text: Users take tirzepatide to cut body fat, with strong appetite suppression creating a larger calorie deficit and a leaner body and face. Trials show some of the largest weight losses of any approved drug; facial leanness and muscle retention are discussed mainly by users.

liraglutide.summary: Daily GLP-1 injection that curbs appetite for fat loss, a milder and older option than semaglutide.

quick.overview:
Liraglutide is a daily GLP-1 injection, sold as Victoza for diabetes and Saxenda for weight management. People use it to reduce appetite and lose body fat.

It activates GLP-1 receptors, which increases fullness and delays stomach emptying, lowering calorie intake. Average losses in trials were roughly 5 to 8 percent of body weight, smaller than with the newer weekly drugs semaglutide and tirzepatide. It was the first GLP-1 drug approved for obesity.
quick.how: It is a prescription daily injection. Some users prefer the daily schedule because it lets them time doses around cravings and meals. It is typically combined with calorie control and training, and weight is commonly regained after stopping.
quick.risks: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are the usual complaints, with gallbladder events, pancreatitis and a raised heart rate reported less often. The label has a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumours seen in rodents, and a risk of kidney injury from dehydration. It requires daily injections and is prescription-only.

angle.text: Liraglutide is a daily GLP-1 injection used to cut body fat by suppressing appetite and creating a calorie deficit, often described as an older, milder option than semaglutide. Weight-loss effects are studied in trials; muscle sparing and dose timing around cravings are discussed by users.

retatrutide.summary: Investigational weekly triple-agonist (GLP-1/GIP/glucagon) with very large trial weight losses that people want for leaning out.

quick.overview:
Retatrutide is an investigational weekly injection from Eli Lilly that activates three receptors: GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon. People interested in it want the largest fat loss yet reported for a drug of this type, with the body and face leaning out.

The GIP and GLP-1 actions reduce appetite, while glucagon-receptor activity is thought to raise energy expenditure and fat burning. Phase 3 results published in 2026 reported mean weight reductions of 17.6, 23.7 and 25.0 percent at 4, 9 and 12 mg after 80 weeks, versus 3.9 percent for placebo. It has no regulatory approval.
quick.how: Within trials it is a weekly injection under study supervision. Outside trials, users source research-labelled vials and some stack it with TRT or anabolics for body recomposition. Trial weight loss accumulated over many months.
quick.risks: Reported trial effects are mainly gastrointestinal and dose-related, with some mild heart-rate increases, and long-term safety is not established. Supplies outside trials are unregulated, with unverified purity, identity and amount, and Lilly has filed lawsuits against black-market sellers. Use outside trials is outside the law in many places. Lean-mass loss and weight regain seen with other drugs of this type are expected here too.

angle.text: Retatrutide is an investigational drug people want for the largest fat loss yet, with triple-receptor appetite and metabolic effects driving a big calorie deficit and a leaner body and face. Trials report very large weight loss; body recomposition and how research vials compare to trial drug are discussed by users.

cagrilintide.summary: Weekly amylin-analogue injection that boosts fullness and lowers food intake, trialled alone and with semaglutide as CagriSema.

quick.overview:
Cagrilintide is a long-acting analogue of amylin, a hormone that signals fullness. People use or follow it as an appetite suppressant for getting lean, alone or alongside semaglutide.

It acts on amylin and calcitonin receptors in the brain, reducing appetite and food intake and slowing stomach emptying. In the REDEFINE 1 study, cagrilintide alone produced a mean body-weight reduction of 11.8 percent versus 2.3 percent for placebo after 68 weeks. A fixed combination with semaglutide, CagriSema, has phase 3 results published in 2025.
quick.how: In trials it is a once-weekly injection. Because its pathway differs from GLP-1, it is paired with semaglutide for additive effect. Outside trials, research-labelled supplies appear on the grey market.
quick.risks: Trial reports describe mainly gastrointestinal effects such as nausea and vomiting, which are dose-related. Long-term safety is still being assessed and it is not approved as a standalone product. Unregulated research-chemical supplies are of unverified quality.

angle.text: Cagrilintide is an experimental amylin analogue used alone or with semaglutide to suppress appetite and cut body fat. It works by boosting fullness signals so you eat less and carry less fat; fat loss is studied in trial populations, while looks-focused "leanmaxxing" use is discussed by users.

setmelanotide.summary: MC4R-targeting injection that reduces hunger and weight in people with specific rare genetic obesity conditions.

quick.overview:
Setmelanotide (Imcivree) is a daily injection approved for obesity caused by rare genetic or acquired disorders of the appetite-control pathway. It appears in fat-loss peptide discussions as an example of targeted pharmacology.

It activates the MC4R receptor in the hypothalamus, a key point in the leptin-melanocortin pathway that controls hunger and energy expenditure. In people whose genetic defect disrupts upstream signalling, this restores fullness signalling, reducing hunger and body weight. It is not approved for ordinary obesity.
quick.how: It is a prescription daily injection for confirmed diagnoses such as POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency, Bardet-Biedl syndrome, or acquired hypothalamic obesity, managed by specialists. Its use is tied to those patient groups rather than general fat loss.
quick.risks: Common effects include injection-site reactions, skin darkening, nausea and spontaneous erections or sexual arousal effects; depression and suicidal thoughts are monitored. It is prescription-only and approved only for specific diagnoses, so use for ordinary fat loss is off-label.

angle.text: Setmelanotide is approved for obesity from rare genetic pathway disorders, where activating the appetite-control pathway reduces hunger and lowers body weight. Its weight effects are studied in those specific patients, and it is mentioned in fat-loss peptide discussions.

tesamorelin.summary: Prescription growth-hormone-releasing peptide that reduces visceral belly fat, approved for HIV-related abdominal fat.

quick.overview:
Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is a synthetic growth-hormone-releasing hormone analogue approved to reduce excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy. Users in physique and peptide circles take it to trim belly fat and raise IGF-1.

It prompts the pituitary to release growth hormone in pulses, raising IGF-1 and promoting fat breakdown, especially visceral fat, which explains the drop in trunk fat in trials. It does not selectively remove cheek or jawline fat, and approval and trial data cover HIV-associated abdominal fat.
quick.how: It is a daily injection by prescription. Off-label users often pair it with ipamorelin for fat loss and IGF-1. Fat returns after stopping.
quick.risks: Reported effects include joint pain, fluid retention, injection-site reactions and glucose intolerance, and raised IGF-1 prompts caution about cancer risk. The label says long-term cardiovascular safety has not been established and it is not indicated for weight loss. It is prescription-only and costly.

angle.text: Tesamorelin raises growth hormone release, which breaks down visceral belly fat and leaves a leaner midsection. It is approved for abdominal fat in HIV lipodystrophy; use in healthy people for physique or facial leanness is off-label.

aod-9604.summary: Growth-hormone fragment sold as a research peptide for fat loss without full growth-hormone effects.

quick.overview:
AOD-9604 is a synthetic peptide based on the fat-metabolising end of human growth hormone, sold as a research peptide for fat loss. Users take it hoping to get leaner without growth hormone's other effects.

It was designed to mimic growth hormone's fat-breaking action without raising IGF-1 or affecting blood sugar. A 12-week randomized trial found participants lost on average 1.8 kg more than placebo, while a later 24-week trial showed poor efficacy and development ended in 2007.
quick.how: It is sold by research-peptide vendors, usually injected, and often stacked with other peptides. Forum users report using it during cutting phases.
quick.risks: Short-term safety in clinical studies was described as similar to placebo, but long-term data are lacking. It is not an approved drug in most countries, is sold as a research chemical of variable quality, and is prohibited in competitive sport by WADA.

angle.text: AOD-9604 is a growth hormone fragment taken as a research peptide to break down stored fat for a leaner body and face without growth-hormone side effects. It has been tested for obesity in humans, with modest results; looks-related effects are reported mainly on forums.

hgh-fragment-176-191.summary: Growth-hormone fragment sold as a research chemical to mobilise fat for cutting, without growth effects.

quick.overview:
HGH Fragment 176-191 is a 16-amino-acid peptide matching the tail end of human growth hormone. Bodybuilders use it as an add-on during cutting phases to mobilise fat the way growth hormone does, without its growth-promoting effects.

In cell and rodent studies the fragment appears to stimulate fat breakdown and reduce fat formation without raising IGF-1 or blood glucose. Its modified relative AOD-9604 was studied in humans; the unmodified fragment itself has not been studied in humans.
quick.how: It is bought as a research chemical and appears in contest-prep logs stacked with other peptides, stimulants and thyroid hormone, usually in the final weeks of a cut.
quick.risks: Human safety data on this peptide are essentially absent. It is unapproved for medical use, comes from unregulated suppliers with unverified purity, and is listed as prohibited by WADA among growth hormone fragments.

angle.text: HGH Fragment 176-191 is used in cutting phases to mobilise stored fat like growth hormone does, aiming for a leaner body and face. The research is laboratory and animal work; human fat-loss data come from its relative AOD-9604.

5-amino-1mq.summary: Small-molecule NNMT inhibitor sold to raise fat metabolism and reduce body fat; studied in cells and mice.

quick.overview:
5-Amino-1MQ is a small molecule that blocks NNMT, an enzyme more active in fat tissue in obesity. Users take it to raise fat metabolism and lose body fat. Despite how it is sold, it is not a peptide.

Blocking NNMT is thought to raise cellular NAD+ levels and shift fat cells toward burning energy. In diet-induced obese mice, NNMT inhibitors of this chemical family reversed weight gain and reduced fat mass, a 2018 finding. No human trial results have been published.
quick.how: It is sold online in oral or injectable forms as a fat-metabolism supplement or research chemical. Users run it alongside diet and training, extrapolating from the rodent findings.
quick.risks: Human pharmacology, dosing and safety are unknown, and no formal toxicity studies exist. It is unapproved, sold with uncertain purity, and its long-term effects on methylation and NAD metabolism have not been evaluated.

angle.text: 5-Amino-1MQ is a gray-market small molecule taken to raise cellular energy metabolism and lose body fat by blocking the NNMT enzyme. Cell and mouse studies show reduced fat gain; human fat-loss and safety data have not been published.

berberine.summary: Plant alkaloid supplement called "nature's metformin" that improves blood sugar and lipids and may support leaner body composition.

quick.overview:
Berberine is a yellow plant alkaloid from goldenseal, barberry and Oregon grape, sold as a supplement. People use it to manage blood sugar, appetite and body fat, and some use it for nutrient partitioning on a bulk or to calm acne.

It activates AMPK, the same cellular energy sensor engaged by metformin, and affects liver glucose output, lipid metabolism and gut microbiota. An umbrella review of 11 meta-analyses found improvements in blood glucose, insulin resistance, lipids and body parameters, though the quality of the underlying analyses needed improvement. Acne and partitioning claims come mainly from users.
quick.how: It is taken as an oral capsule, usually with meals, as part of a fat-loss or metabolic-health routine alongside diet and training. Effects on glucose and weight in trials build over weeks.
quick.risks: Gastrointestinal upset such as cramping, diarrhoea and constipation is most common. It inhibits CYP3A4 and other enzymes and may interact with drugs including ciclosporin and some diabetes medicines. It is generally avoided in pregnancy and in newborns because of jaundice concerns. The FDA issued warning letters to supplement makers about berberine marketing claims between 2020 and 2022; product quality varies.

angle.text: Berberine improves how the body handles glucose, which users take to reduce fat gain, improve nutrient partitioning during bulks and sometimes calm acne for leaner, clearer looks. Trials show modest effects on glucose, lipids and weight; the acne and partitioning claims come mainly from users.

l-carnitine.summary: Supplement that carries fatty acids into mitochondria for energy; sold as a fat burner and recovery aid.

quick.overview:
L-carnitine is a compound the body makes and also gets from red meat, sold as a supplement for fat loss, recovery and energy. Users take it to push more fat toward being burned for fuel.

It carries long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria where they are oxidised for energy. A 2020 meta-analysis of 37 randomized trials with 2,292 participants reported small average reductions in body weight, body mass index and fat mass. Healthy people generally make enough of it themselves.
quick.how: It is taken as oral capsules or powder (often L-carnitine tartrate or acetyl-L-carnitine), or in liquid and injectable forms by some users, alongside training and a calorie deficit. Effects reported in studies are small and appear over weeks.
quick.risks: Intakes of about 2 to 3 g daily are generally tolerated, with nausea, diarrhoea and a fishy body odour at higher intakes. Gut bacteria convert carnitine to TMAO, which is associated with cardiovascular risk in observational studies, though causality is unresolved. It is sold as an unscheduled supplement.

angle.text: L-carnitine is taken as a fat burner and recovery aid, on the logic that moving fatty acids into mitochondria means more fat used for energy and less body fat. Trials show small, variable weight effects; injected versions and recovery claims come mainly from users.

egcg.summary: Green tea catechin sold as a fat burner that slightly raises calorie burn, usually alongside caffeine.

quick.overview:
EGCG is the most abundant catechin in green tea, sold as a concentrated extract in fat-burner and pre-workout products. Users take it for a small extra calorie burn and slightly lower body fat.

It may modestly raise energy expenditure and fat oxidation by prolonging noradrenaline signalling and may reduce fat absorption in the gut. Trials and meta-analyses of green tea catechins show small effects on weight and fat mass, varying with caffeine intake and baseline habits. Some users speculate about muscle effects via myostatin, an idea based on lab findings.
quick.how: It is taken as a capsule or extract, often before workouts and combined with caffeine-based thermogenics and L-carnitine. Brewed green tea is another route.
quick.risks: Concentrated extracts, especially on an empty stomach, have been linked to rare liver injury; in 2018 the European Food Safety Authority said 800 mg or more daily from supplements could raise liver-damage risk. The FDA issued warning letters to EGCG supplement makers between 2008 and 2017. It can reduce iron absorption and interact with some drugs. Brewed tea is considered safe.

angle.text: EGCG is a green tea extract taken as a fat burner, where a slightly higher metabolism adds a small extra calorie burn and slightly lower body fat. Studies show small thermogenic effects with mixed results; the muscle-building talk comes from lab findings and users.

capsaicin.summary: Chili pepper compound taken for a slight bump in calorie burn and lower appetite as part of fat-loss routines.

quick.overview:
Capsaicin is the compound that makes chili peppers hot, and it is sold in capsules as a thermogenic and appetite supplement. People use it for a small metabolic and appetite boost during fat loss, and it comes up in discussions of lip plumping and facial leanness.

It activates the TRPV1 channel on sensory neurons, triggering sympathetic nervous system activity that raises heat production slightly, and it may affect fullness signalling and brown fat. Small human studies show modest rises in energy expenditure and fat oxidation; a 2014 meta-analysis found weak evidence that taking it before a meal might slightly reduce food intake.
quick.how: It is eaten as chili in food or taken as capsule supplements and chili extracts in thermogenic products, alongside diet and training. Effects are small and show up gradually.
quick.risks: Oral use can cause stomach pain, burning, nausea and diarrhoea, and may worsen reflux. Topical capsaicin burns and irritates, and contact with eyes or broken skin is painful. It is legal and unscheduled as food and supplement.

angle.text: Capsaicin from chili peppers gives a mild rise in energy expenditure and slightly lower appetite, which users add to fat-loss diets for a small contribution to leanness. Human studies show slight effects on energy use; the lip-plumping and facial-leanness claims come from users.

creatine-monohydrate.summary: Low-cost, extensively studied supplement that helps you train harder and build strength and muscle size.

quick.overview:
Creatine monohydrate is a baseline supplement in physique circles, used to build strength and muscle size and to support high-intensity training. More muscle gives a fuller, more powerful frame.

Muscle stores creatine as phosphocreatine, which quickly regenerates ATP during short, intense efforts. Supplementation raises muscle creatine, which can allow slightly more work per session and may encourage greater adaptation over time. A 2018 review named it the most effective supplement for increasing high-intensity exercise capacity and muscle mass, and a 2024 meta-analysis of adults under 50 found greater strength gains than placebo. Part of the early scale-weight rise is water drawn into muscle cells.
quick.how: It is taken daily as a flavourless powder mixed into a drink, alongside resistance training. Gains build over weeks, and it is often combined with a protein-rich diet and other basics like whey.
quick.risks: It is legal and sold over the counter. Reviews of long-term use in healthy people report it is generally well tolerated, with water retention and occasional stomach upset the most common complaints. It can modestly raise serum creatinine without necessarily reflecting kidney damage, and people with kidney disease are advised to seek medical advice first. Some people are non-responders. Claims about hair loss via DHT have been examined by researchers and remain debated.

angle.text: Creatine gives your muscles more ATP for hard sets, so you train harder and build more muscle and strength over time. Its muscle and strength effects are among the best studied of any supplement; claims about hair loss and kidney damage are debated.

whey-protein.summary: Fast-digesting milk protein that makes it easy to hit protein targets, build muscle and stay lean while dieting.

quick.overview:
Whey protein is a powder made from the liquid left over from cheese making, and it is a complete protein rich in leucine. Lifters and dieters use it to reach daily protein targets, build muscle and hold on to lean mass while cutting, which supports a leaner, more muscular look.

It raises blood amino acids quickly, and leucine switches on muscle protein synthesis through mTORC1 signalling. A 2018 meta-analysis of 49 trials found protein supplementation during resistance training modestly increased strength, fat-free mass and muscle size. The benefit comes mainly from adding to total daily protein, so it is similar to other protein sources when intake is already adequate.
quick.how: It is mixed into shakes, oats or other food, often after training or between meals, as a convenient way to add protein. Concentrate, isolate and hydrolysate forms are available; muscle gain builds over months of training.
quick.risks: Whey is a food product and legal everywhere. Lactose intolerance or milk allergy can cause digestive symptoms, and isolates contain less lactose. Some forum posters link whey to acne, an association with some observational support. Quality varies by brand, and people with kidney disease are advised to follow medical guidance.

angle.text: Whey supplies fast protein with leucine, which feeds muscle protein synthesis so you build more muscle and keep it while dieting for a leaner physique. Muscle gain from adequate protein is well studied; some users link whey to acne, an association with some observational support.

leucine.summary: The amino acid that switches on muscle-growth signalling (mTOR); used in drinks and meals to support muscle protein synthesis.

quick.overview:
Leucine is an essential branched-chain amino acid found in meat, dairy, eggs and soy, also sold as a powder or in BCAA and essential amino acid products. Users add it to drinks or meals to trigger muscle-growth signalling, and compare protein sources by their leucine content.

Intracellular sensors such as Sestrin2 respond to leucine and release inhibition of mTORC1, promoting muscle protein synthesis. Most clinical work on leucine-enriched products has been in older adults with sarcopenia, with mixed results. Adding isolated leucine to an already adequate protein intake has limited evidence of extra muscle in healthy trainees.
quick.how: It is taken as a powder in drinks around training or added to meals low in protein, or consumed through high-leucine foods and whey. It is typically combined with resistance training and sufficient total protein.
quick.risks: Leucine is a normal dietary component and legal. High supplemental amounts can cause digestive upset and may disturb the balance of other branched-chain amino acids, and it is hazardous for people with maple syrup urine disease.

angle.text: Leucine activates mTOR signalling, which drives muscle protein synthesis and more muscle growth, so users add it to drinks and meals. The acute signalling is well studied; extra leucine on top of adequate protein has limited evidence of added muscle.

beta-alanine.summary: Pre-workout ingredient that buffers muscle acid so you get more high-rep work; the tingles are harmless.

quick.overview:
Beta-alanine is an amino acid that builds carnosine in muscle, sold as a powder or capsule and a staple of pre-workout blends. Users take it to get more reps out of hard, high-rep sets, expecting more training stimulus for muscle.

Taking it for several weeks raises muscle carnosine, which buffers hydrogen ions that build up during intense exercise and delays fatigue. Meta-analyses of placebo-controlled trials report small average benefits, concentrated in efforts of about one to four minutes. It does not directly build muscle tissue, and effects on single maximal efforts are small.
quick.how: It is taken daily as a powder or capsule, often in pre-workout products, with benefits building over several weeks. Divided or slow-release forms are used to reduce tingling.
quick.risks: Paraesthesia, a harmless tingling of the skin, is the main reported side effect. It is legal, not banned in sport, and long-term data in healthy adults show no clear toxicity at studied intakes.

angle.text: Beta-alanine raises muscle carnosine, which buffers acid in hard sets so you can get more reps and a bigger training stimulus. Studies show performance gains in high-intensity efforts; direct effects on muscle size are less established, and the tingling is a known harmless side effect.

hmb.summary: Leucine metabolite used to limit muscle breakdown and speed recovery, especially during cuts or hard training.

quick.overview:
HMB is a metabolite of leucine, sold as a calcium salt or free acid. Lifters use it to preserve muscle during cuts and recover faster, and some call it a steroid alternative, a comparison the research does not support.

It is thought to reduce protein breakdown through the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway and support muscle repair. Results depend on who is studied: meta-analyses report more often positive results in older adults and clinical conditions, while trained athletes show small effects. The ISSN position stand says chronic intake appears safe for up to at least a year.
quick.how: It is taken as a daily capsule or powder, often during calorie restriction or intense training blocks, alongside enough protein. It is also used in clinical nutrition supplements for older and ill patients.
quick.risks: HMB is legal with a good short-term safety record in trials, and reported side effects are minor, mostly gastrointestinal. Trials in experienced trainees eating enough protein have generally not found clear benefits, and product quality varies.

angle.text: HMB is a leucine metabolite that limits muscle breakdown, which lifters use to recover faster, train with more volume and retain muscle during cuts. Studies show benefits mainly in untrained or older people or during illness; effects in trained lifters are mixed.

citrulline-malate.summary: Pre-workout ingredient that raises nitric oxide for a bigger pump, better blood flow and a few more reps.

quick.overview:
Citrulline malate combines L-citrulline with malic acid and is a common pre-workout ingredient. Users take it for a muscle pump, fuller-looking muscles, endurance in resistance sets and less soreness.

Citrulline is converted to arginine in the kidney, raising nitric oxide production and widening blood vessels, so more blood reaches working muscle. Meta-analyses report a small improvement in repetitions to failure with low certainty, and single trials often show no effect. No study in the sources reviewed has shown it increases muscle size.
quick.how: It is taken as a powder in pre-workout drinks before training, sometimes paired with tadalafil for blood flow. Pump effects are noticed within sessions.
quick.risks: It is legal and generally well tolerated; the main complaint is stomach upset at larger amounts. It can lower blood pressure slightly, which matters for people taking antihypertensive or erectile dysfunction drugs.

angle.text: Citrulline malate raises nitric oxide and blood flow for a bigger pump and a few more reps, giving more training stimulus and a fuller look in the gym. Studies on reps and endurance are mixed, and effects on long-term muscle growth have not been shown.
